messages.author: 92a06be4d96a96ee
messages.subject: customized boxplot function and new ggplot2
parts:
I have been using a ammended version of Kohske's code from
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3010403/jitter-if-multiple-outliers-in-ggplot2-boxplot

To which I add an additional argument for outlier.alpha. However, with
the new ggplot2 release, its giving me an error. The first error:

Error in eval.with.vis(expr, envir, enclos) :
  could not find function "proto"

Is due to the name spacing of the new ggplot and is fixed with
library(proto). Then the error becomes:

Error in proto(GeomBoxplot, { : object 'GeomBoxplot' not found

That can be fixed by using ggplot:::GeomBoxplot to access the
unexported function. However, then the final assignment:

geom_boxplot_jitter_outlier <- GeomBoxplotJitterOutlier$build_accessor()

errors with:

Error in get(x, envir = this, inherits = inh) :
  object 'build_accessor' not found

Now, I'm at a loss!! The custom geom code is below as is my sessionInfo().

GeomBoxplotJitterOutlier <- proto(GeomBoxplot, {
   draw <- function (., data, ..., outlier.colour = "black",
outlier.shape = 16,
    outlier.size = 2, outlier.jitter=0,outlier.alpha=1) {
# copy the body of function 'draw' above and paste here.
defaults <- with(data, data.frame(x = x, xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
        colour = colour, size = size, linetype = 1, group = 1,
        alpha = 1, fill = alpha(fill, alpha), stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    defaults2 <- defaults[c(1, 1), ]
        if (!is.null(data$outliers) && length(data$outliers[[1]] >=
        1)) {
            pp<-position_jitter(width=outlier.jitter,height=0)
            p<-pp$adjust(data.frame(x=data$x[rep(1,
length(data$outliers[[1]]))], y=data$outliers[[1]]),.scale)
        outliers_grob <- GeomPoint$draw(data.frame(x=p$x, y = p$y,
colour = I(outlier.colour),
            shape = outlier.shape, alpha = outlier.alpha, size = outlier.size,
            fill = NA), ...)
    }
    else {
        outliers_grob <- NULL
    }
    with(data, ggname(.$my_name(), grobTree(outliers_grob,
GeomPath$draw(data.frame(y = c(upper,
        ymax), defaults2), ...), GeomPath$draw(data.frame(y = c(lower,
        ymin), defaults2), ...), GeomRect$draw(data.frame(ymax = upper,
        ymin = lower, defaults), ...), GeomRect$draw(data.frame(ymax = middle,
        ymin = middle, defaults), ...))))

}

  objname <- "boxplot_jitter_outlier"
  desc <- "Box and whiskers plot with jittered outlier"
  guide_geom <- function(.) "boxplot_jitter_outlier"

})

geom_boxplot_jitter_outlier <- GeomBoxplotJitterOutlier$build_accessor()

Hi,

ggplot2 0.9 includes large internal changes, so this kind of hack as
is will not work with 0.9.

You can update the function, but you need to know the internal structure.
You may ask @wch or @hadley to update the geom_boxplot to make
jittering if there are multiple outliers ;-p

kohske

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: customized boxplot function and new ggplot2
parts:
Another possibility is to plot the boxplot with hidden outlier points (using colour=NA), and then plot the outliers separately using geom_dotplot.

In the example below, I ripped out the code to do box plot calculations from stat_boxplot(), and simplified it. (Note that ggplot2's stat_boxplot does calculations slightly differently from the base graphics boxplot.) I think this does the right thing, but I can't guarantee that it works perfectly.

# This returns a data frame with the outliers only
find_outliers <- function(y, coef = 1.5) {
  qs <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)
  stats <- as.numeric(quantile(y, qs))
  iqr <- diff(stats[c(2, 4)])
  
  outliers <- y < (stats[2] - coef * iqr) | y > (stats[4] + coef * iqr)

  return(y[outliers])
}


library(MASS)  # Use the birthwt data set from MASS

# Find the outliers for each level of 'smoke'
library(plyr)
outlier_data <- ddply(birthwt, .(smoke), summarise, lwt = find_outliers(lwt))


# This draws an ordinary box plot
ggplot(birthwt, aes(x = factor(smoke), y = lwt)) + geom_boxplot()


# This draws the outliers using geom_dotplot
ggplot(birthwt, aes(x = factor(smoke), y = lwt)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA) +
  geom_dotplot(data = outlier_data, binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center",
               binwidth = 4)


You'll probably want to tweak 'binwidth' for your particular case.

Hope this helps! It's not a standard-looking boxplot, but it's probably less ugly than jittering the outliers.

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: customized boxplot function and new ggplot2
parts: One more quick note. geom_dotplot draws circles with a fill and outline -- 'fill' and 'colour' respectively. When the points are this tiny, the outline can make them look like they're mushed together. You can remove the outline and make the dots look more distinct by setting 'colour=NA'.

ggplot(birthwt, aes(x = factor(smoke), y = lwt)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = NA) +
  geom_dotplot(data = outlier_data, binaxis = "y", stackdir = "center",

binwidth = 4, colour = NA)

Bear in mind that on some platforms, the resulting circles might not be antialiased, and thus look jagged and asymmetrical.

-Winston
